summary: Prioritize specific, counter-intuitive visual scenarios (e.g., 'A 10kg lead sphere') over abstract 'Why does...' questions in the first 3 seconds.
Shift the hook structure from 'Have you ever wondered...' or 'You've used [X] your whole life...' to a 'What happens if...' narrative.
Eliminate academic titles that list the full topic; use high-arousal punctuation and specific questions instead.
Aim for a tighter hook-to-explanation transition; long setups cause viewer drop-off even when engagement is high.
Focus on 'Immediate Visual Proof' in the first 5 seconds to boost stayed_pct above the 40% barrier.
winning_hooks: A 10kg lead sphere and a 1kg lead sphere dropped from the same height in a vacuum. Why don't they hit the ground at different moments?
Why does baking soda fizz the moment it hits vinegar?
avoid: Starting with 'You've seen/used/done [X] your whole life, but why...'
Explaining common household chemical reactions with purely linguistic setups.
Lengthy, multi-sentence hook preambles that exceed 15 words before addressing the core phenomenon.
next_experiment: A/B test the current 'Why' question format against a 'Stop doing [common action] or [result] happens' format to see if fear/urgency increases the stayed_pct.
